Policies and Initiatives.title: Rs 4,869 crore for Ladakh; Leh Palace among heritage sites to be developed
Policies and Initiatives.summary: The Union government has allocated Rs 4,869.31 crore to Ladakh for 2026-27, a decrease from the previous year's revised allocation. The budget will fund revenue and capital expenditure, establishment costs, and various schemes focused on infrastructure and socio-economic development. The allocation will also support the development of heritage sites, including the Leh Palace.

Policies and Initiatives.title: Union Budget 2026: Jammu and Kashmir fund allocation ‘marginally’ up; Ladakh sees around 27% increase
Policies and Initiatives.summary: The Union Budget 2026 has allocated a marginally increased fund to Jammu and Kashmir, with a modest increase of ₹2,000 crore. Ladakh, on the other hand, has seen a significant increase of around 27% in its fund allocation. The increased allocation for Jammu and Kashmir is considered insufficient to address the region's developmental gap and revive existing industrial units.

Policies and Initiatives.title: Ladakh gets Rs 4,869.31 crore allocation in Union Budget 2026–27
Policies and Initiatives.summary: The Indian government has allocated Rs 4,869.31 crore for Ladakh in the 2026-27 Union Budget, comprising Rs 2,542.26 crore for revenue and Rs 2,327.05 crore for capital expenditure. This allocation is lower than the revised Rs 7,377.43 crore allocated in 2025-26. Ladakh, a Union Territory since 2019, will receive this funding for its development.

Policies and Initiatives.title: Union Budget 2026: Mountain, turtle, birdwatching trails to come up in Himachal, Jammu & Kashmir, Odisha, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu
Policies and Initiatives.summary: The Union Budget 2026 will fund the development of mountain, turtle, and birdwatching trails in several Indian states, including Himachal, Jammu & Kashmir, Odisha, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu. A birdwatching trail will be specifically developed along the Pulicat Lake on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border. These projects aim to promote eco-tourism in these regions.
